messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High 5xx error rate detected in cluster model-serving-prod-eu-west-1. Metric: http.5xx.rate > 6% over 1m. Pager: sre-oncall. Links: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/3167774444 :rotating_light:
alice: oncall here, I'm seeing the same in the dashboard. escalation P1?
devon: I get crash traces from model-runner pods, repeated SIGSEGV + OOM before segfault in logs. Posting snippet.
devon: ```
[runner][ERROR] runtime: page alloc fail: KVCACHE eviction triggered, mlock failed
SIGSEGV at 0x7ff... pc=0x...
stack: model_runner+0x1f2d, kvcache+0x8b
```
maya: which model variants are hit? any dedicated customers?
devon: mostly open-model-7b-quant and a few custom quantized variants. Dedicated customer traffic low so far. Hosteds taking bulk.
liz: CS: customers A and C reported increased errors and 10-20s timeouts for embedding calls ~ few minutes ago. Jordan on call with A.
jordan-cs: yup i'm on slack with customer A, they're seeing 502s and retries. asked for ETA.
alice: ok immediate mitigations: 1) route traffic away from eu-west-1 to eu-central and us-west as fallback for non-data-residency routes 2) scale up fallback model (fp16 variant) and enable graceful routing 3) drain affected nodes and restart model-runner service 4) enable temporary higher-retry on client side to avoid client-side failover storms.
devon: can we flip routing with the gateway? I can push a quick policy: prefer-region eu-central for model=open-model-7b-quant with fallback to open-model-7b-fp16.
alice: do it. tag me when done.
devon: pushing policy now. command: ```infra route update --cluster model-serving-prod --from eu-west-1 --to eu-central --model open-model-7b-quant --fallback open-model-7b-fp16 --weight 0.7```
devon: policy applied. checking traffic shift. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Route change applied by devon at 2026-03-15T03:08:12Z. Old traffic weight eu-west-1:0.9 -> 0.2. New: eu-central:0.7.
alice: great. next, let's drain runners on nodes with high crash counts. devon, can you taint/drain?
devon: starting drain on node gpu-eu-12 and gpu-eu-17. command: ```kubectl cordon gpu-eu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-eu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```
devon: restarting model-runner daemonset on those nodes: ```kubectl rollout restart ds/model-runner -n inference```
devon: also disabling quantization-specific kernel (quant-attn-v2) as candidate root cause. toggling rollout to use generic attention kernel.
maya: is there evidence quant kernel misbehaving?
devon: stack traces reference quant_attention.cu in backtrace repeatedly. memory fragmentation + async eviction looks like it trips a race leading to segfaults during KV cache compaction.
liz: CS update: customer A acknowledges route to eu-central and is test-calling, still sees 502s occasionally but numbers improving.
jordan-cs: they asked for ETA on full recovery. I told them 20-30m while we drain and stabilize.
alice: monitoring shows 5xx dropping from 6.8% -> 3.2% since route change and restarts. still elevated but trending down.
devon: logs show fewer SIGSEGVs on rolled nodes. restarting remaining affected nodes now.
ops-bot: Restart jobs submitted: 4/6 nodes restarted.
alice: good. open incident ticket: INC-2026-3142 created, linking runbook: https://confluence.redwood/incident-runbooks/model-runner-segfaults
devon: temporary hotfix applied: switch model runner to conservative GC + disable async KV eviction flag `--kv-evict=sync`. will watch.
maya: any customer data exposure or loss?
alice: no evidence of data leakage. errors are internal 5xx from runtime crashes; requests either retried or routed. need to confirm any queued user requests lost—looking at ingress logs.
devon: ingress shows ~0.6% requests dropped due to in-flight connection resets during the peak, mostly short window. CS notified.
liz: noted, CS updated customers A and C, tentatively ok with planned follow-up postmortem.
jordan-cs: customer A asked for SLA credit estimate — sending to bizops.
alice: continue monitoring. timeline: 03:07 alert -> 03:09 routing -> 03:12 drain start -> 03:18 5xx down to 3.2% -> 03:24 hotfix applied -> 03:30 baseline near 0.7%.
ops-bot: Alert suppressed: http.5xx.rate below threshold for 2 consecutive minutes.
alice: I'm going to hand this to morning shift for post-incident follow-up and RCA. @devon pls prepare logs and a short summary of suspected root cause (quant kernel + KV eviction race) and mitigation steps committed.
devon: will dump stack traces, reproduce with small harness, and prepare patch to quant-attn kernel.
liz: I'll coordinate customer comms and keep tickets open.
maya: operations action items: increase model-runner watchdog memory threshold, set kv-evict to sync by default for 7b quant variants, add canary for quant kernel changes, and add autoscaling buffer for eu-west-1.
alice: assign followups: 1) devon - patch quant kernel (due EOD) 2) ops - change default kv eviction (due EOD) 3) eng-sre - postmortem (due +48h) 4) cs - customer summary (due +4h).
jordan-cs: customer A happy with timeline, wants copy of postmortem when available.
alice: handing off to devon and ops for cleanup. I'll mark incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. If we get regressions re-open pager.
devon: handing off, I'll document commands and gcore outputs in the incident ticket.
jordan-cs: thanks team, I'll update customer chat. :pray:
alice: closing slack thread from oncall perspective, moving to incident doc for follow-up. final note: root cause suspected memory-fragmentation triggering quant kernel segfault during KV eviction; mitigation was routing, draining, restart, and conservative runner flags.
